about: Eyes on the sides of the head (horse, cow, deer).
rules: An almond about 1.6-2 times as wide as it is open (2.5-3 when relaxed), its long axis rising 10-25 degrees from the inner corner to the outer.
The upper lid is the heavier: its dark edge runs 1-2 texels into the lid, then fades to the coat over 3-4; a crease above it; the lower lid narrower and softer, fading over 4-5.
The inner corner is a low sharp point holding the darkest texels of the eye, with a soft streak 3-5 texels down and forward from it (the tear trough).
The lids are a deeper, more saturated shade of the skin, never black; one bright catchlight in the upper front quarter.
